We model a decision impact pathway is for farmstands or connecting farms to workers as general interventions for sustainable food environments in urban Hanoi, Vietnam. 

# Urban Hanoi farmstand 

Simulation of the farmstand intervention options:

```{r mcsimulation, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# Source our model
source("company_model.R")

# Ensure consistent results with the random number generator
# not for each 'run' of the MC simulation but for 
# consistency each time we run the entire simulation 
set.seed(84)

# Monte Carlo simulation 
source("functions/mcSimulation.R")

company_simulation_results <- mcSimulation(
  estimate = estimate_read_csv("data/company_input.csv"),
  model_function = company_model,
  numberOfModelRuns =  1e4, #run 10,000 times
  functionSyntax = "plainNames"
)

```

The Net Present Value (i.e. current value of the future benefits). Here we plot the distribution for the decision and frame the projected NPV. 

```{r plot_dist_boxplot, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# plot distributions for the two options
source("functions/plot_distributions.R")
Fig_distributions <- plot_distributions(mcSimulation_object = company_simulation_results, 
                   vars = c("decision_farmstand", "decision_connectFarm"),
                   old_names = c("decision_farmstand", "decision_connectFarm"),
                   new_names = c("NPV farmstand vs. baseline", "NPV connect farm vs. baseline"),
                   method = 'boxplot', 
                   base_size = 7,
                   x_axis_name = "Comparative NPV outcomes over five years")

ggsave("figures/Fig_distributions.png", width = 15, height = 8, units = "cm") 

```

## Summary of results for the decision

```{r summary_decisions, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# Summary for private school passive and STEM gardens
summary(company_simulation_results$y[1:2]) 
```

```{r percentiles_decision_farmstand, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# Calculate the 5th and 95th percentiles for farmstand
quantile(company_simulation_results$y$decision_farmstand, probs = c(0.05, 0.95))
```

```{r percentiles_decision_connectfarm, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# Calculate the 5th and 95th percentiles for connectfarm
quantile(company_simulation_results$y$decision_connectFarm, probs = c(0.05, 0.95))
```

## Projection to Latent Structures (PLS)

We use Projection to Latent Structures (PLS) model to assess the correlation strength and direction for model variables and outcome variables. The Partial Least Squares is fitted with the orthogonal scores algorithm with `pls::plsr`.


```{r pls_farmstand}

source("functions/pls_model.R")
pls_result <- pls_model(object = company_simulation_results,
                resultName = names(company_simulation_results$y)[1],  
                                ncomp = 1)
# read in the common input table
input_table <- read.csv("data/company_input.csv")

plot_pls_farmstand <- plot_pls(plsrResults = pls_result, 
                            input_table = input_table, 
                            threshold = 0.9) + 
  theme(legend.position = "none", axis.title.x = element_blank(), 
  axis.text.x = element_blank(),
  axis.ticks = element_blank()) + scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 7)) + ggtitle("PLS Farmstand") + 
  annotate(geom="text", x=5, y=2, label="Farmstand")

#For farmstand with formal STEM education
pls_result_connect<- pls_model(object = company_simulation_results,
                  resultName = names(company_simulation_results$y)[2], # the "NPV_garden_STEM" 
                                ncomp = 1)

plot_pls_connect <- plot_pls(plsrResults = pls_result_connect, 
                          input_table = input_table, 
                          threshold = 0.9) + 
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 7)) + 
  annotate(geom="text", x=5, y=2, label="Farm connect")

Fig_pls <- plot_pls_farmstand / plot_pls_connect 

ggsave("figures/Fig_pls.png", width=6, height=4) 
```

## Value of Information

Here we assess value of information with the `multi_EVPI` function. We calculate value of information in the form of Expected Value of Perfect Information (EVPI).

```{r mc_table, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

mcSimulation_table <- data.frame(company_simulation_results$x, 
                                 company_simulation_results$y[1:2])

# # List of NPV variables to move to the last position (calculate 2 EVPIs only)

# 
# # Move NPV variables to the last position
# mcSimulation_table <- mcSimulation_table %>% select(-all_of(npvs_to_move), all_of(npvs_to_move))

```

Calculate EVPI:

```{r evpi-general_calc}

# evpi <- decisionSupport::multi_EVPI(mc = mcSimulation_table, 
#                                     first_out_var = "decision_farmstand")
#  save as a local .csv (takes ~ 20 minutes to run this)
#  save(evpi,file="data/data_evpi.Rda")
  load("data/data_evpi.Rda")
# open from saved file (last model run) - it is stable result / takes very long to run 

```

EVPI :

```{r evpi_farmstand}
#Value of information 
source("functions/plot_evpi.R")
plot_evpi_farmstand <- plot_evpi(EVPIresults = evpi,
                            decision_vars = "decision_farmstand",
                            new_names = "Farmstand",
                          input_table = input_table,
                          threshold = 10, 
                          min_evpi = 1) +
theme(legend.position = "none", axis.title.x = element_blank()) # +
# scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 210))


plot_evpi_connectfarm <- plot_evpi(EVPIresults = evpi,
                            decision_vars = "decision_connectFarm",
                            new_names = "Connect farm",
                          input_table = input_table,
                          threshold = 10, 
                          min_evpi = 0.02) +
theme(legend.position = "none") # +
# scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 210))

Fig_evpi <- plot_evpi_connectfarm | plot_evpi_farmstand

ggsave("figures/Fig_evpi.png", width = 30, height = 8, units = "cm")
```

## Input data for the simulations 

### Summary

Here we provide a summary of the garden intervention options. We do this with a summary table of the simulation results. We show the percentage of missing values as well as the mean, median and standard deviation (SD) for each output of our model simulations. We use the `gt_plt_summary()` from {gtExtras} and with options from {svglite}. The table shows the  name, the plot overview as well as the number of missing values, the mean, median and the standard deviation of the distribution for all variables that were fed into the model from our input table of uncertainty values. 

```{r gtExtras_summary_x, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# Subset the outputs from the mcSimulation function (y) to summarize only on the variables that we want.
# names(garden_simulation_results$x)
mcSimulation_table_x <- data.frame(company_simulation_results$x[4:7]) #, 21:30, 32:41, 43:70, 73:76)  also of possible interest

 gtExtras::gt_plt_summary(mcSimulation_table_x) 
# a summary table with missing, mean, median and sd

```

The table shows the variable name, the plot overview as well as the number of missing values, the mean, median and the standard deviation of the distribution for variables that calculated in the model.
